title: Cellular competency hides genome quality from selection, driving an intelligence ratchet

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Cellular competency hides genome quality from selection, driving an intelligence ratchet

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because competent biological material compensates for defects, selection cannot see genome quality clearly, so more evolutionary change accrues in competency mechanisms than in structural components, producing a positive-feedback intelligence ratchet based on remapping information to new contexts.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 6. What It Means, and What Next: A Research Program for Further Development

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The competency of our material means that selection cannot see the quality of genomes clearly46. More evolutionary work thus has to be conducted on the competency mechanisms, not the structural components, leading to a positive feedback loop—an intelligence ratchet based on the remapping of information to new contexts47.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue”, Entropy (Basel, Switzerland) (2024), doi:10.3390/e26060481; section “6. What It Means, and What Next: A Research Program for Further Development”. Scope: Evolution of multicellular organisms; in silico evolutionary models

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-memory-13: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.43

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The ratchet makes measurable predictions in models, and some existing simulations may permit analysis. Its organism-wide evolutionary interpretation is underspecified and difficult to distinguish from robustness, drift and network-complexity alternatives.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In evolutionary simulations, vary compensatory competency while holding mutation and selection regimes fixed, and measure selection gradients on structural versus competency loci over time. The proposed ratchet predicts weaker selection on structural quality and increasing investment in compensatory mechanisms.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Simulation confirmation may reflect model assumptions.

Comparative genomic evidence does not directly expose historical selection visibility.

Competency and structural loci must be imposed by the modeler.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public coding sequences support a weak proxy, a comparison of substitution rates between putative control genes and structural genes. They do not record whether selection can see genome quality, nor whether change preferentially accumulates in competency mechanisms because of a feedback ratchet. The historical mechanism stays underdetermined by the sequence data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare evolutionary rates of genes that implement physiological compensation, such as ion channels and gap-junction components, with rates of structural and housekeeping genes, across multicellular phylogenies. Faster evolution of the competency class would be consistent with the ratchet; equal or slower rates would weaken it. Blindness of selection and positive feedback are not identified by the rate comparison alone.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Rate differences have many causes besides selection failing to see defects.

Competency mechanism is not a gene class that genomes label.

The ratchet itself is an evolutionary model without a public run that isolates the feedback loop.
